target_claim: Let \(\lambda\in\mathbb Q\) satisfy \(0\neq |1+\lambda|\neq1\), let \(k\in\mathbb N\), and suppose \(\mathcal A\) is a randomized \(2^{N^k}\)-approximation algorithm for \(I(\lambda)\): on every input graph \(H\) having \(N\) nodes, it runs in time polynomial in \(N\) and returns \(\mathcal I(H;\lambda)\in\mathbb Q\) such that \(\Pr[2^{-N^k}I(H;\lambda)\leq\mathcal I(H;\lambda)\leq2^{N^k}I(H;\lambda)]\geq3/4\). Let \(G=(V,E)\) have \(|V|=n\), and choose a positive integer \(l\) as follows. If \(|1+\lambda|>1\), put \(x=(1+\lambda)^l-1\), require \(|x|\geq2^{n^{k+1}}\), and let \(G_l\) be obtained by cloning every vertex of \(G\) exactly \(l-1\) times; hence \(|V(G_l)|=nl\) and \(I(G;x)=I(G_l;\lambda)\). If \(0<|1+\lambda|<1\), put \(x=\lambda/(1+\lambda)^l\), require \(|x|\geq2^{n^{k+1}}\), and let \(G_l\) be obtained by performing an \(l\)-comb at every original vertex, where an \(l\)-comb adds \(l\) new degree-one neighbors to that vertex; hence \(|V(G_l)|=n(l+1)\) and \(I(G;x)=(1+\lambda)^{-l|V|}I(G_l;\lambda)\). Define \(\mathcal I(G;x)=\mathcal I(G_l;\lambda)\) in the cloning case and \(\mathcal I(G;x)=\mathcal I(G_l;\lambda)/(1+\lambda)^{l|V|}\) in the comb case. The claim is that applying \(\mathcal A\) to the enlarged input \(G_l\) yields \(\Pr[2^{-n^k}I(G;x)\leq\mathcal I(G;x)\leq2^{n^k}I(G;x)]\geq3/4\), with the approximation exponent computed from \(n=|V(G)|\), rather than from the number of nodes \(|V(G_l)|\) in the graph actually supplied to \(\mathcal A\). Here \(I(G;x)\) is the independent-set polynomial used in the source, whose degree \(c\) is the maximum independent-set size and which is written as \(I(G;x)=Nx^c+\sum_{0\leq j\leq c-1}i(G;j)x^j\), with \(N\) the number of independent sets of maximum size.
source_quote:
Let $\lambda \in \QQ$. By a randomized $2^{n^k}$-approximation
  algorithm for $I(\lambda)$ we mean a randomized algorithm, that,
  given a graph $G$ with $n$ nodes, runs in time polynomial in $n$ and
  returns $\II(G;\lambda)\in \QQ$ such that
  \begin{equation*}
    \Pr[2^{-n^k}I(G;\lambda) \leq \II(G;\lambda) \leq
  2^{n^k}I(G;\lambda)] \geq \frac{3}{4}.
  \end{equation*}

Fix some $k$. Given a graph $G$, the graph $G_k$ is obtained by
cloning each vertex of $G$ exactly $k-1$ times. Note that the result
of the cloning is independent of the order in which the different
vertices are cloned. For $a\in V(G)$ let $a_1, \ldots, a_k$ be the
corresponding vertices in $G_k$.

Let $G$ be a graph and $G_k$ be obtained out of $G$ by cloning each
vertex of $G$ exactly $k-1$ times. Then it holds
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:P_clone}
P(G_k;u,x)=P(G;u, (1+x)^k-1).
\end{equation}

Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph, $a\in V$ some vertex and $V':=V\setminus
\{a\}$. Then we define the $k$-comb of $G$ at $a$ as $G_{a,k}=(V\uni
\{a_1, \ldots, a_k\}, E\uni \{ \{a,a_1\}, \ldots, \{a,a_k\} \})$, with
$a_1, \ldots, a_k$ being new vertices.

We can perform a $k$-comb operation at every $a\in V$ and call the
result $G_k$. After substituting $x$ for $x_v, v\in G_k$, we obtain
$p(k,u,x) = (1+x)^k(xu^2+1) - xu^2$ and
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:combtrans}
P(G_k;u,x) =
p(k,u,x)^{|V(G)|}P(G;u,x/p(k,u,x)).
\end{equation}

Assume we have $\lambda, 0\neq |1+\lambda|\neq1$, $k\in \N$ and a
  randomized $2^{n^k}$-approximation algorithm $\aA$ for $I(\lambda)$.

Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph with $|V|=n$. We distinguish two cases. If
  $|1+\lambda|>1$, we choose a positive integer $l$ such that with
  $x:=(1+\lambda)^l-1$ we have
  \begin{equation}
    \label{eq:large_point}
    |x|\geq  2^{n^{k+1}}.
  \end{equation}
  This can be achieved by choosing $l=\poly(n)$. (Let $m$ be an
  integer such that $|\lambda+1|\geq 2^{1/(n^m)}$. Then we can choose
  $l=(n^{k+1}+1)n^m$.) If $0<|1+\lambda|<1$, we choose a positive
  integer $l$ such that with $x:=\frac{\lambda}{(1+\lambda)^l}$ we
  have \eqref{eq:large_point}.  By Theorem~\ref{thm:p2p}
  (\eqref{eq:combtrans} in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:comb}, resp.)
  we have $I(G;x)=I(G_l;\lambda)$ ($I(G;x)=(1+\lambda)^{-l|V|}
  I(G_l;\lambda)$, resp.). Algorithm $\aA$ returns on input $G_l$
  within time $\poly(nl)=\poly(n)$ an approximation
  $\II(G_l;\lambda)$, such that with $\II(G;x):=\II(G_l;\lambda)$
  ($\II(G;x):=\frac{\II(G_l;\lambda)}{(1+\lambda)^{l|V|}}$, resp.) we
  have
  \begin{equation}
    \label{eq:approx}
    2^{-n^k}I(G;x)\leq \II(G;x)\leq 2^{n^k} I(G;x)
  \end{equation}
  with high probability.

Let $c$ be the maximal independent set size of $G$ and $N$ be the
  number of independent sets of maximal size. We have
  \begin{align*}
    I(G;x) = Nx^c + \sum_{0\leq j\leq c-1}i(G;j)x^j
  \end{align*}
